analysis: The PR is documentation-only. In docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md the only changed line is 689, a gpt-oss-20b row in the checkpoint-size table. It now describes bf16 K/V on all 24 layers: 3.15 MB fixed state, 25.17 MB per 1,024 tokens, 154.1 MB file at 6,144 tokens. In docs/reference/configuration.md the changes are the last-updated date and a sentence stating that MLX_QUANTIZED_CONSTANT_CACHE does not apply to a bf16 GPT-OSS checkpoint. No source code, key handling, encryption, cacheSalt scoping, TTL, HMAC naming, authorization or routing logic is changed. The T-041 controls (HMAC-keyed lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, account-scoped cacheSalt, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch, KEK purge, storage validation) are not altered by these edits. The smaller documented per-checkpoint sizes only describe layout and could lower an operator's estimate of staging or disk footprint. They are documentation of the claimed behavior; the supplied evidence does not show any code change that affects the at-rest surface or the staging-cap and endurance budgets. The accuracy of the bf16 claim depends on code outside this PR, so I did not verify it. Residual question for integration: whether a companion code change in another PR alters the GPT-OSS KV dtype or the checkpoint size, and thus the endurance, disk and staging limits. Nothing in this batch is evidence of that. The patch excerpt for configuration.md is truncated, but the changed-range map is complete (lines 3 and 593) and shows no further changes.
